newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, in California, fights for every vote.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, in California, fights for every vote.

text.p: President Bill Clinton, upbeat after his debate with rival Bob Dole, on Thursday sought to shore up his support in California as a confident aide said Republicans were now waging a fight "about survival."
Clinton campaigned is southern California -- a state where various polls suggest his once overwhelming lead has shown signs of slippage -- urging voters to "show up" on Election Day.

Addressing an enthusiastic crowd of several thousand outside the county court house in Santa Ana, Clinton said he enjoyed the 90-minute televised exchange with Dole because it let him talk about the future and let Americans "go beyond the tired rhetoric of yesterday's politics."

Clinton and Dole squared off for their final debate before the Nov. 5 election on Wednesday night at the University of San Diego, with opinion polls suggesting the Republican's more aggressive attacks on the incumbent did little to win over voters.

A USA Today/CNN/Gallup poll found that 59 percent of Americans felt Clinton won the debate, while 29 percent said Dole was the winner. An ABC News poll found 56 percent of respondents saying Clinton won, while 27 percent said Dole carried the day.

Douglas Sosnik, the White House political director, said Clinton was taking nothing for granted in the final weeks. "We're going to continue to hammer away .. the election's not over. We want to make sure we keep the states we've got," he said.
The president and his aides clearly were buoyed by the debate as Clinton's campaign focused on southern California.

A statewide poll published on Wednesday by the San Francisco Examiner found that 49 percent of likely California voters back Clinton while 37 percent supported Dole. Reform Party candidate Ross Perot and the Green Party's Ralph Nader each had 3 percent. Eight percent were undecided.
Clinton's lead of 12 points was down four points from a similar poll in September.

"The big question in 19 days is: Who's going to show up?" Clinton said in urging his supporters to vote. "I talk a lot about our responsibility, it is your responsibility to go vote, your responsibility as a citizen, your responsibility to be there."
Private surveys show Clinton leading in states that produce well over the 270 electoral college votes to win, while the Clinton campaign concedes Dole has about 52 electoral votes at this point.

Asked if pride was a motivating force behind the rival campaign, Clinton's political director Sosnik was asked if the rival camp was being driven out of pride. "No, I think right now that this is not about pride," he said. "I think this is about survival."

In what amounted to a symbolic gesture to show his determination to win the state, Clinton visited Orange County, a highly conservative area where voters traditionally have favoured the Republican politics of Ronald Reagan over anything Democrats have offered.
Clinton then went to Los Angeles for fund-raising events that will raise $3 million for the Democratic party and congressional candidates.

The president was to return early on Friday to Washington, where he and campaign officials will reassess the situation heading into the final weeks of the re-election fight and decide their priorities.

Aides say Clinton has already made clear that he intends to campaign in states like Florida and Texas that traditionally have been conceded to Republicans in the past, in part because he hopes to assist Democrats running in congressional races.
